competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 20-F Item 4 Business Overview.
competitive_position.claim: As of December 31, 2025, Frontline owned a fleet of 80 vessels (41 VLCCs, 21 Suezmax tankers, 18 LR2/Aframax tankers) with an aggregate capacity of approximately 17.6 million DWT, giving it scale to negotiate competitive terms with suppliers and charterers.

We also believe that the size of our fleet is important in negotiating terms with our major clients and charterers. We also believe that our large fleet enhances our ability to obtain competitive terms from suppliers, ship repairers and builders and to produce cost savings in chartering and operations.

The global tanker fleet continued to age during the year. The average age of the crude tanker fleet reached approximately 14 years, the highest level in more than two decades.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in both the Business Overview and Risk Factors of the 20-F.
competitive_position.claim: The tanker industry is highly cyclical, with volatility in profitability, charter rates, and asset values driven by supply and demand changes, meaning Frontline's competitive position and earnings can deteriorate rapidly in a market downturn.
quotes: The tanker industry is highly cyclical, experiencing volatility in profitability, vessel values and freight rates.

Historically, the tanker industry has been highly cyclical, with volatility in profitability, charter rates and asset values resulting from changes in the supply of, and demand for, tanker capacity and changes in the supply of and demand for oil and oil products.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 20-F Risk Factors section.
competitive_position.claim: An over-supply of tanker capacity, if new deliveries exceed scrapping and conversions, could materially reduce charter rates, vessel values, and Frontline's profitability and ability to service debt.
quotes: If the capacity of new vessels delivered exceeds the capacity of tankers being scrapped and converted to non-trading tankers, tanker capacity will increase. If the supply of tanker capacity increases and the demand for tanker capacity does not increase correspondingly, charter rates could materially decline. A reduction in charter rates and the value of our vessels may have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, our ability to pay dividends and our compliance with current or future covenants in any of our agreements.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 20-F Risk Factors, citing IEA and OPEC forecasts as referenced in the filing.
competitive_position.claim: A shift in consumer demand from oil toward alternative energy sources could materially adversely affect Frontline's future performance; the IEA forecasts peak oil in 2030 while OPEC forecasts continued growth through at least 2050.
quotes: While the International Energy Agency ("IEA") forecasts "peak oil", the year when the maximum rate of extraction oil is reached, to be 2030 and OPEC forecasts global oil demand to continue to grow through at least 2050, a shift in consumer demand away from oil and oil products could have a material adverse effect on our future performance, results of operations, cash flows and financial position.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 20-F Risk Factors section.
competitive_position.claim: If competitors build vessels that are more efficient, more flexible, or use more environmentally sustainable propulsion technologies, they could command higher charterhire payments and reduce the resale value of Frontline's vessels.
quotes: Our vessels have an average age of 7.5 years as of December 31, 2025, and if new vessels are built that are more efficient or more flexible or have longer physical lives than our vessels or utilize more environmentally sustainable propulsion technologies, competition from these more technologically advanced vessels could adversely affect the amount of charterhire payments we receive for our vessels and the resale value of our vessels could significantly decrease.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 20-F Item 5 Market Overview, drawing on EIA, Fearnleys, Clarksons Research, and Kpler data; the March 2026 US-Iran strikes are described in the same section.
competitive_position.claim: Geopolitical sanctions and conflict have reshaped tanker market dynamics: by year-end 2025 approximately one-fifth of the global crude and product tanker fleet was sanctioned by at least one major authority, and the allocation of tonnage has shifted toward fewer owners controlling a larger share of the fleet, which the company expects to partially offset scheduled newbuilding deliveries.
quotes: By year-end, approximately one-fifth of the global crude and product tanker fleet was reported to be sanctioned by at least one major authority.

The allocation of tonnage among market participants has shifted meaningfully, with fewer owners now controlling a larger share of the global fleet. Coupled with a rapid ageing fleet, we expect these structural supply constraints to partially offset scheduled newbuilding deliveries, creating a manageable net fleet growth.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 20-F Risk Factors; the counter-point is stated in the 20-F Item 4 ESG section.
competitive_position.claim: Frontline faces increasing ESG scrutiny from investors, lenders, and market participants; failure to meet evolving ESG standards could lead to reputational damage, litigation costs, and restricted access to debt and equity capital markets, impairing its ability to finance growth.
quotes: Companies which fail to adapt or to comply with investor, lender or other industry shareholder expectations and standards, which are evolving, or which are perceived to have failed to respond appropriately to the growing concern with ESG issues, regardless of whether there is a legal requirement to do so, may suffer from reputational damage, costs related to litigation, and the business, financial condition, and/or stock price of such a company could be materially and adversely affected.
certain investors and lenders may exclude oil transport companies, such as us, from their investing portfolios altogether due to ESG factors.

Together with a constructive crude demand outlook and anticipation of further replacement of sanctioned volumes transferring to the compliant fleet, we expect the fundamentals for compliant tankers to remain favorable going forward.

material_events.claim: Frontline entered into a Framework Agreement with CMB.TECH to purchase 24 VLCCs for an aggregate purchase price of $2,350.0 million; deliveries of all 24 vessels were completed by the first quarter of 2024.
quotes: On October 9, 2023, Frontline entered into a Framework Agreement (the "Framework Agreement") with CMB.TECH NV (formerly Euronav NV) ("CMB.TECH"). Pursuant to the Framework Agreement, the Company agreed to purchase 24 VLCCs with an average age of 5.3 years, for an aggregate purchase price of $2,350.0 million from CMB.TECH (the "Acquisition").

The Company took delivery of the 13 remaining vessels in the first quarter of 2024 and drew down $518.7 million under its $1,410.0 million senior secured term loan facility with a group of relationship banks and $60.0 million under its subordinated unsecured shareholder loan to partly finance the deliveries.
